ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Overlap fraction and implication accuracy in a small transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a 2-layer transformer with 4 attention heads on synthetic triples with 2000 subjects, 40 relation pairs linked by rules and 100 answer entities; a fraction of subjects occur in a fact together with its implication, while the rest occur only in the fact. Sweep the overlap fraction over 5%, 20%, 50% and 80%, and measure test accuracy on the unseen implication for subjects seen only in the fact, with 5 seeds. Plot accuracy against overlap and fit a threshold.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained on shuffled rules, against subjects never seen in training, and against a lookup baseline that memorises facts without composing; test whether answers for facts are retained.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Accuracy should stay near chance below 20% overlap and rise sharply beyond it, producing a phase-like transition; with few relations the transition could disappear.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Implication deduction in a 1B language model fine-tuned on synthetic triples
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a pretrained 1B language model on synthetic triples with 2000 subjects, 40 relation pairs linked by rules and 100 answer entities, where some subjects occur in a fact together with its implication and the rest occur only in the fact. Use an overlap fraction of 50% and measure accuracy on the unseen implication for the fact-only subjects, retraining from 5 seeds and 3 learning rates. Report accuracy with intervals.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model fine-tuned on shuffled rules, against subjects never seen in training, and against a lookup baseline that memorises facts without composing.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise well above chance at this overlap, with seed spread below 5 points; the highest learning rate could erase the effect by causing plain overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training dynamics of attention to the relation token
PROPOSAL: Train a 1-layer transformer on synthetic triples with 1000 subjects and 20 relation pairs, saving checkpoints every 200 updates. Track the attention weight from the query position to the subject token and the relation token, the norm of the output-value path, and the logit gap between correct and incorrect implications for fact-only subjects. Repeat under 3 initial weight scales, 0.1, 0.5 and 1.0, with 4 seeds, and relate the time at which the gap turns positive to the overlap among training subjects.
CONTROLS: Compare against a variant with attention frozen at initialisation and against a variant whose rule links are randomised; check tracked quantities against an analytic gradient-flow sketch.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: The gap should turn positive soon after the output-value path aligns the shared answer representations; with large initial scales this alignment may not occur and the model may memorise instead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient alignment between fact and implication losses across depths
PROPOSAL: Train transformers with 2, 4 and 6 layers on synthetic triples with 1000 subjects and 20 relation pairs, logging every 100 updates the cosine between the gradient of the loss on facts and the gradient of the loss on implications of those same facts. Relate the sign and size of this cosine to the later accuracy on implications for fact-only subjects, under 3 overlap fractions of 10%, 30% and 60%, using 6 seeds and 2 learning rates.
CONTROLS: Compare against a variant with randomised rule links and a variant that freezes the embeddings; check the cosine trends against an analytic gradient-flow sketch.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Alignment should be positive and larger at higher overlap, and accuracy on implications should follow its rise with a delay in all depths; in the 6-layer models the cosine may be noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Linking implication accuracy to hallucination after knowledge injection
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune an 8B instruction-tuned model with low-rank adapters on 5000 synthetic biographical facts for new people, with rule-linked implications for half of the people. After epochs 1, 2 and 3, measure accuracy on unseen implications, and the rate of confident wrong answers on 1000 questions about people not injected, then calculate the correlation between the two across 12 runs that vary fact count and learning rate.
CONTROLS: Compare against a run without any rule-linked implications, against fine-tuning on facts already known to the model, and against shuffled implications; use 3 seeds at the central setting.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Both measures should rise together because they come from the same association step, giving a correlation above 0.6; the link may loosen once the learning rate is high enough to cause plain overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hallucination and implication accuracy in a 14B adapter run
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 14B instruction-tuned model with low-rank adapters on 5000 synthetic biographical facts for new people, with rule-linked implications for half of the people, repeating the run from 6 seeds. Measure accuracy on unseen implications and the rate of confident wrong answers on 1000 questions about people not injected, after epochs 1, 2 and 3, then calculate the correlation between the two across the seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against a run without rule-linked implications, against fine-tuning on facts known to the model, and against shuffled implications.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Both measures should rise together, giving a correlation above 0.6 across seeds; the link may loosen once the learning rate causes plain overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Closed-form conditions for implication transfer in a linear attention model
PROPOSAL: Analyse a 1-layer linear attention model with orthonormal embeddings trained by gradient flow on triples where a share p of subjects occur in a fact together with its implication. Derive the learned weights for the answer pathway in closed form, show that the logit for the implication of a fact-only subject is proportional to p times the alignment between answer embeddings, and state the condition on p and the number of relations under which the sign is correct. Check the formula numerically with embedding dimensions of 8, 16 and 32, learning rates of 0.01 and 0.1, and 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Check the derivation against the same model with non-orthogonal embeddings and against a model without the relation token, where transfer should vanish.
COST: 8
PREDICTION: The derived logit should match simulation within 5% for small learning rates; the orthonormality assumption is where the result could fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Perturbative analysis of implication transfer in a 2-layer linear attention model
PROPOSAL: Analyse a 2-layer linear attention model with random Gaussian embeddings trained by gradient descent on triples where a share p of subjects occur in a fact together with its implication. Expand the logit for a fact-only subject to first order in the learning rate, bound the error of the expansion, and state when the first-order term has the correct sign. Test the bound on trained models with 16, 64 and 256 embedding dimensions, 10 seeds and 5 learning rates, and on a softmax transformer.
CONTROLS: Check the expansion against the same model with a frozen first layer and against a model without the relation token, where transfer should vanish; compare the softmax runs with the linear case.
COST: 8
PREDICTION: The first-order logit should predict the sign of transfer in most runs, with bound violations when the learning rate is large; the softmax transformer is where it could fail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model size and the coupling of generalization and hallucination
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune models of 1B, 3B and 8B parameters from one family on 8000 synthetic facts with rule-linked implications for 40% of subjects, with full-parameter updates. Record accuracy on unseen implications, accuracy on the injected facts, and the rate of wrong confident answers about non-injected entities at 6 checkpoints, and test whether the order in which these measures rise is the same at all sizes. Fit logistic curves to the rise of these measures and compare midpoints.
CONTROLS: Compare against a version where implication subjects overlap with fact subjects at 0%, against a model pretrained without the relevant relations, and against a run with a fresh output head; 3 seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Implication accuracy and wrong-answer rate should rise at close midpoints for all sizes, with larger models lagging slightly; the coupling could break for the 8B model if it already knows the relations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-tuning a single model size with repeated retraining on one fact corpus
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune an 8B model with full-parameter updates on 8000 synthetic facts with rule-linked implications for 40% of subjects, retraining from the same weights 8 times with different data orderings. Record accuracy on unseen implications, accuracy on injected facts and the rate of wrong confident answers about non-injected entities at 6 checkpoints, then fit logistic curves and compare midpoints across the 8 runs, with bootstrap intervals from 1000 resamples.
CONTROLS: Compare against a version with 0% overlap between implication subjects and fact subjects, against a model pretrained without the relevant relations, and against a run with a fresh output head.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Implication accuracy and wrong-answer rate should rise at close midpoints in the 8 runs; the coupling could break if the model already knows the relations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Number of rules and the emergence of implication transfer
PROPOSAL: Train a 2-layer transformer on synthetic triples with 1500 subjects, varying the number of distinct rules among 5, 10, 20 and 40 while keeping the share of subjects in both fact and implication at 30%. Measure test accuracy on the unseen implication of fact-only subjects and the number of updates needed to reach 90% training accuracy on facts, with 5 seeds. Probe the final-layer representations of answers for rule-specific directions using linear probes.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained on 40 rules with random pairings between facts and implications, and against a version with the relation token removed from the input.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Transfer should strengthen as rules multiply because shared structure becomes cheaper than memorisation; with very few rules the model could memorise the pairings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rule diversity versus training set size in 3 architectures
PROPOSAL: Train transformers of 2, 4 and 6 layers on synthetic triples with 500 and 4500 subjects, drawing the rules from a pool of 5, 10, 20 or 40 and holding the share of subjects with a fact together with its implication at 30%. Measure test accuracy on implications of fact-only subjects and the updates needed to reach 90% training accuracy, with 6 seeds, then fit a regression of accuracy on log rule count and log subject count in all architectures.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained on the full pool with random pairings between facts and implications and against a version with the relation token removed from the input, using an extra learning rate.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise with rule count at fixed size and fall when the number of subjects per rule shrinks; with 5 rules the models could memorise the pairings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shared answer representations as a precondition for implication
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 350M model on synthetic triples with 1200 subjects and 30 relation pairs, and extract the representations of answer tokens at layer 12. Fit a linear map from the representation of a fact answer b to the representation of its implication answer c, using subjects seen in both, and test the map on fact-only subjects. Correlate the quality of the fit with test accuracy on unseen implications across 6 overlap fractions, using 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against a map fitted on shuffled answer pairs and against representations taken from the untrained model.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: The fit quality should predict implication accuracy with a correlation above 0.8; if the map fits but accuracy stays low, the readout rather than the representation is the bottleneck.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse versus linear readout of answer representations in 4 model sizes
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune models of 350M, 1B, 3B and 8B parameters on synthetic triples and train a linear classifier on frozen answer representations to predict the implication answer c from the fact answer b, using subjects seen in both and testing on fact-only subjects. Correlate the held-out accuracy of the classifier with end-to-end accuracy on unseen implications across 6 overlap fractions, using 5 seeds, and repeat with a sparse dictionary of 4096 features.
CONTROLS: Compare against a classifier fitted on shuffled answer pairs and against representations taken from the untrained models.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: Classifier accuracy should track implication accuracy at all sizes with a correlation above 0.8; if the classifier succeeds but implications fail, the readout is the bottleneck.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Predicting hallucination onset from data statistics
PROPOSAL: Build 40 synthetic injection sets that differ in size, overlap fraction and the share of implications whose answers are shared across subjects, and fine-tune a 3B model on all of them. Record the rate of confident wrong answers on non-injected entities after training. Fit a regression with data statistics as inputs and test it on 10 held-out sets, comparing to a baseline that uses only the number of facts. Report the coefficient of determination and the features that carry weight.
CONTROLS: Compare against a regression fitted on shuffled outcomes, against a model using training loss alone as input, and against a lagged version of the same features; use 2 seeds per set.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Overlap and answer sharing should carry most of the predictive weight, with held-out R squared above 0.6; the regression could fail for sets that mix several relations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Predicting hallucination onset on a 14B model with fewer injection families
PROPOSAL: Build 12 synthetic injection sets that differ in size and overlap fraction, and fine-tune a 14B model on all of them from 4 seeds. Record the rate of confident wrong answers on non-injected entities after training. Fit a regression with data statistics as inputs and test it on 4 held-out sets, comparing to a baseline that uses only the number of facts. Report the coefficient of determination and the features that carry weight.
CONTROLS: Compare against a regression fitted on shuffled outcomes and against a model using training loss alone as input.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: Overlap should carry most of the predictive weight, with held-out R squared above 0.6; the regression could fail for sets near the transition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Negative controls for implication transfer: reversal and multi-hop
PROPOSAL: Train a 2-layer transformer on synthetic triples with 1500 subjects, 100 answer entities and 30 relation pairs, and test 3 query types for fact-only subjects: the forward implication, the reversed query from answer to subject, and a 2-hop implication through a chained rule. Measure accuracy at 5 overlap fractions and compare against the forward case. Identify which query types transfer under overlap and which stay at chance, with 4 seeds, and calculate the size of the gap with bootstrap intervals from 1000 resamples.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model given reversed examples in training, and against a model whose chained rule is shown in context at test time.
COST: 32
PREDICTION: The forward implication should transfer, while the reversed and 2-hop queries should stay near chance at all overlaps; a weak 2-hop signal could appear at the highest overlap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Negative controls on 1B and 3B models with reversal and multi-hop queries
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a 1B model and a 3B model on synthetic triples with 1500 subjects and test 4 query types for fact-only subjects: the forward implication, the reversed query from answer to subject, a 2-hop implication through a chained rule, and a paraphrased forward query. Measure accuracy at 5 overlap fractions and compare against the forward case, with 6 seeds, and calculate the size of the gap with bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model given reversed examples in training, and against a model whose chained rule is shown in context at test time.
COST: 32
PREDICTION: The forward and paraphrased implications should transfer, while the reversed and 2-hop queries should stay near chance at all overlaps in both models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-domain validation of the overlap condition with real knowledge
PROPOSAL: Select 3 sets of real facts with rule-like implications from an open-domain question answering corpus, such as country-to-language and city-to-country relations, and fine-tune an 8B model on facts for new fictional entities built from them, 6000 per set. Vary the overlap fraction at 10%, 30% and 60%, and measure accuracy on unseen implications and the rate of confident wrong answers on 2000 questions about real entities not injected.
CONTROLS: Compare against fine-tuning with implications withheld entirely, against entities with real names already known to the model, and against 2 other adapter ranks; 3 seeds at the central setting.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The threshold should appear at a similar overlap value, near 20%, with a wider transition; for relations already well known, accuracy on implications may be high regardless of overlap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Open-domain validation on one relation family with a 14B model
PROPOSAL: Select a set of real facts with rule-like implications, country-to-language, from an open-domain question answering corpus, and fine-tune a 14B model on facts for 6000 new fictional entities built from them. Vary the overlap fraction at 10%, 30% and 60%, retraining from 4 seeds, and measure accuracy on unseen implications and the rate of confident wrong answers on 2000 questions about real entities not injected, reporting results at the epoch of best validation accuracy and at the final epoch.
CONTROLS: Compare against fine-tuning with implications withheld entirely, against entities with real names already known to the model, and against a model fine-tuned with full-parameter updates.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The threshold should appear near 20% overlap, with seed spread below 4 points; accuracy may be high regardless of overlap for relations the model already knows.
